correct_completion: had more time to prepare for the exam.
full_sentence: I wish I had more time to prepare for the exam.
acceptable_variants: could spend more time preparing for the exam.
wish I had more time to prepare for the exam.

options.text: will have more time to prepare for the exam.
options.why_wrong: 'I wish' expresses an unreal present situation, while 'will' describes a real future plan, which contradicts the wish.

options.text: had more time to prepare for the exam.
have more time to prepare for the exam.
options.why_wrong: After 'wish', the present tense does not express an unreal present; the past form 'had' is needed.

options.text: had more time yesterday to prepare for the exam.
options.why_wrong: The past time reference 'yesterday' conflicts with the present meaning of the wish, which describes the current situation.

grammar_focus: Unreal present wishes with 'wish' followed by the past simple
explanation: After 'wish', a past form signals an unreal present situation rather than a past event. Ukrainian speakers may choose a present form here because Ukrainian expresses wishes with a different verb construction, so the English past form can feel unfamiliar.
translation: Я б хотів, щоб у мене було більше часу, щоб підготуватися до іспиту.
